title: GUIDE: Group Equality Informed Individual Fairness in Graph Neural Networks

problem.claim: Graph neural networks may make biased decisions against underprivileged groups or individuals in critical decision-making scenarios.

gap.claim: Existing individual-fairness methods optimize overall individual fairness but disregard equality of individual fairness between groups, producing different fairness levels among groups.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes GUIDE, a GNN framework for group-equality-informed individual fairness.
GUIDE operates on individuals' similarity matrix to learn personalized attention for individual fairness without group-level disparity.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe GUIDE as a novel GNN framework.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that comprehensive experiments on real-world datasets show a good balance between group-equality-informed individual fairness and model utility.
The authors provide an open-source implementation of GUIDE.

narrative_sequence.summary: GNNs are increasingly used in critical decision-making because of their performance and end-to-end design.
GNNs may make biased decisions, motivating fairness notions such as individual fairness.
Existing individual-fairness methods overlook equality of fairness across groups, leading to disparate group-level fairness.
GUIDE targets individual fairness together with equalized fairness levels across groups using personalized attention over an individual-similarity matrix.
The authors report favorable fairness-utility balance on real-world datasets and release an implementation.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, metrics, numerical results, or experimental settings.
The abstract does not define the personalized-attention mechanism or optimization procedure in detail.
The abstract does not report limitations, computational costs, or reproducibility details beyond an implementation link.
